data.description:
## Context / Problem

Teams that run more than one tracker project against a single codebase — or several repos against a
single rebar ticket store — cannot use rebar's bridge today. It is hard-wired to exactly one project
at three independent points: `JiraConfig.project` is a single scalar (`src/rebar/_config_schema.py:482-484`);
the inbound fetcher builds its JQL pair from one key and fails closed on an empty one
(`jqls_for`, `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py:78-90`); and the applier aborts an entire
pass if any outbound update or delete targets a key outside that one project (`CrossProjectTargetError`,
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/applier.py:217-258`). The only escape today is a destructive one-way
re-target script (`scripts/retarget_jira_project.py`) that clears every binding and re-creates every issue.

Assignee preservation for tracker-unresolvable users is a stated requirement of this work but is
already owned by in-progress bug `9b94-af9e-4acf-4dff`, whose open acceptance criterion is precisely
"decide the intended semantics". That decision is recorded there and this epic takes it as a
dependency rather than duplicating it as a child.

## Approach

Model the many-to-many as one shared ticket store sitting between N repos and N tracker projects,
rather than as N bridges or per-repo project lists. Each ticket records the project it syncs into and
the repos it belongs to.

The **store**, not the repo, owns the project set — a mapping at `.bridge_state/projects.json` on the
tickets branch, alongside the shared bridge state already committed there (`bindings.json`,
`prev_snapshot.json`). This is the decisive choice and the reason for it is mechanical:
`prev_snapshot.json` is the reconciler's last-known-remote state, so if two repos fetched different
project subsets against one shared snapshot, each pass would see the other's projects as vanished from
the remote and diff them as deletions. Making the project set a store property removes that failure
mode by construction rather than guarding against it, and leaves no per-repo list that could disagree.

Everything is built on the provider-neutral `bridge` verb group (epic `2f79-2b32-28c5-4eb3`, which
chose that noun specifically because other trackers are planned) and on the existing backend-neutral
port — `RemoteRef(vendor, instance, remote_id)` and `Backend.project` / `Backend.query_project`
(`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend.py:610-632`). `Backend.project` is already documented as
"the backend's effective write/create project scope", so it serves as the per-repo default for
rebar-created tickets with no new config key, and the model generalizes to trackers beyond Jira
without a second design.

Migration for existing client stores writes **no events**. The project field is tri-state — absent
means legacy, explicit-empty means never sync, an explicit key means sync there — mirroring the
established `file_impact_scope` undeclared/none/paths pattern (`docs/ticket-model.md:210-212`). The
bridge resolves absent against the legacy default recorded in the mapping. An idempotent check-then-act
ensure unit seeds that mapping (`docs/migrations.md:40-56`), which is the sanctioned seam; the ordered
School-A ledger is explicitly not built (`docs/migrations.md:14-16`). Writing an EDIT per ticket was
rejected: on a store of this size that is a four-figure event write under the store write lock, and the
MCP-boot entry point deliberately runs the sweep on a short lock budget and skips when contended
(`docs/migrations.md:63-65`), so an event-writing migration would silently skip at one of its three
entry points.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/` — the project mapping store, fetch fan-out, outbound dispatch,
  and the cross-project guard.
- `src/rebar/_store/ensures.py` and `src/rebar/_store/init.py` — the ensure unit that seeds the mapping.
- `src/rebar/_store/compat.py` — the conditional capability stamp.
- `src/rebar/reducer/`, `src/rebar/schemas/ticket_state.schema.json`, `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py`,
  `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py`, `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py` — the two new ticket fields and their
  create-time arguments.
- `src/rebar/_cli/` — the `bridge projects` subcommand.
- `docs/` — the multi-project model, the mapping, and an ADR.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `bridge projects` lists, sets and removes project→repos entries on the store mapping, and the
      same operations exist on the library and MCP surfaces; checked by a per-surface test asserting
      each of the three surfaces reads back an entry written by another.
- [ ] A store whose mapping holds two projects fetches both in a single pass and each ingested ticket
      records the project it came from; checked by a reconciler test asserting one JQL pair is issued
      per configured project and asserting the recorded project on each created ticket.
- [ ] A ticket whose project is explicitly empty produces no outbound mutation; checked by an
      outbound-differ test asserting an empty mutation list for that ticket while a sibling with a
      project produces one.
- [ ] A ticket created with an explicit project targets that project rather than the repo default;
      checked by a dispatch test asserting the create call carries the ticket's project.
- [ ] An outbound update targeting a project inside the configured set proceeds while one outside it
      still raises `CrossProjectTargetError`; checked by a paired applier test covering both directions.
- [ ] Every ticket in a pre-feature store resolves to the recorded legacy default with zero events
      written; checked by a migration test asserting the store's event count is byte-identical before
      and after the sweep and that each ticket resolves to the default.
- [ ] A store whose mapping holds more than one project carries `multi-project-bridge` in
      `.store-compat.json` `required_capabilities` and a binary lacking that capability refuses writes,
      while a single-project store remains writable; checked by a store-compat test covering both.

## Child decomposition

Each responsibility below owns a disjoint set of files so children can be worked without edit
conflicts:

- **The project mapping store** — the `.bridge_state/projects.json` record, its read/write helpers
  under the existing bridge-state concurrency, and the ensure unit that seeds it from the current
  backend project as the legacy default. Delivers the migration and legacy-default criteria.
- **The `bridge projects` command surface** — the subcommand under the `bridge` group plus the library
  and MCP parity that epic `2f79` requires of every bridge verb. Delivers the first criterion.
- **The ticket project field** — schema, CREATE event data, reducer projection, and the create-time
  argument across CLI, library and MCP, including the promote-only rule that refuses to change the
  project of a ticket that already holds a binding. Delivers the empty-project criterion.
- **The ticket repos field** — schema, reducer projection, its create-time argument, and the inbound
  defaulting that fills it from the mapping for tickets arriving from a tracker.
- **Multi-project inbound fetch** — fan-out over the configured projects and snapshot union, keeping
  the existing per-query truncation ceiling scoped per project rather than shared. Delivers the
  two-project fetch criterion.
- **Multi-project outbound dispatch** — per-ticket project on create and the relaxation of the
  cross-project guard from a single configured project to set membership. Delivers the explicit-project
  and guard criteria.
- **The store-compat capability stamp** — the conditional `required_capabilities` entry and its
  fail-closed read path. Delivers the final criterion.
- **Documentation and ADR** — the multi-project model, the mapping, the tri-state field, and the
  architectural decision record.

## Compatibility and rollback

The change is additive at every layer. An absent project field means legacy, so a pre-feature store
behaves exactly as it does today and needs no operator action. A single-project store never receives
the capability stamp and therefore stays readable and writable by older binaries; only a store that has
actually gone multi-project fails closed on them, which is the intended protection — an older binary
would otherwise fetch its one project, see the other projects' tickets as unbound, and create duplicate
issues in the wrong project.

Rollback is per-change on Gerrit. The mapping file and the capability entry are inert to older binaries
apart from the deliberate fail-closed, and deleting `.store-compat.json` returns every binary to the
ABSENT implicit-legacy pass-through, with the idempotent ensure unit re-stamping it on the next covered
write by a current binary (`docs/migrations.md:197-203`).
data.title: Many-to-many tracker projects: per-ticket bridge project + repo association over one shared store
